_about: Amp look + About / Tips cards for the AMP block and the factory cabs (design: Sonicake CFW/SmartBox/RE/cfw/design/webapp_amp_cab_info.md). Keys = effect_library.json ids. DRAFT texts: fact-check and listen on the pedal before a release.

301.about: Small, raw and touch-sensitive: it breaks up early and cleans up with your pick attack and the guitar volume.
301.heardOn: Blues, roots rock, raw garage crunch.
tips: Gain 55–70 for a gritty edge that still follows your hands.
One knob does it all: lower it with bright single coils.

302.about: The tweed amp that became the template for the first British rock heads: full, warm and generous in the low end.
tips: Gain 50–65; Bass under 50 keeps it tight.
B-Man B is the same amp on the brighter input.

303.about: Big, loud and clean: the reference for glassy American cleans, with scooped mids and lots of headroom. Pedals sit on it very well.
303.heardOn: Country, funk, pop cleans, pedal platform.
tips: Gain 30–45 stays clean with any pickup.
On for humbuckers, off for bright single coils.

304.about: The plain AC30 channel: warm, slightly dark and compressed, with a smooth breakup when pushed.
tips: Turn it on to open the top end.

305.about: A transistor amp famous for staying clean at any volume: crisp, flat and hi-fi. A great base for chorus and delays.
305.heardOn: New wave, jazz, clean pop and funk.
tips: Middle around 50; Bright on for sparkle.
An A-Chorus in FX2 for the classic stereo shimmer.

306.about: The first British rock head: warm, round and touch-sensitive, with a soft, singing crunch.
tips: Under 50 for a darker, vintage voice.

307.about: Two channels linked together for a fatter, more aggressive crunch: the classic late-60s rock sound. Gain 1 and Gain 2 blend the two inputs.
tips: Gain 2 a little under Gain 1 adds weight without mud.
Both gains 60–75 for big rock rhythm.

308.about: The classic 80s rock head: one channel, a master volume and a preamp that bites hard in the upper mids. Tight and aggressive, it cleans up well when you roll back the guitar volume.
308.heardOn: 80s hard rock and metal, punk, classic crunch rhythm.
tips: Gain 55–70, Middle 60. For more, add a Boost or the Scream drive in front instead of more gain.
Adds top-end sparkle; keep it under 60 with bright pickups.

309.about: The Bassman on its bright input: more bite and presence, cuts through a band more easily.
tips: B-Man N is the same amp, warmer.

310.about: Jangly, chiming highs and a soft, compressed breakup. The Top Boost channel adds treble and bass; Cut tames the top end.
tips: Turn it up if the highs feel harsh with bright pickups.

311.about: The crunch side of a legendary hot-rodded head: thick, harmonically rich and very responsive.
tips: Gain 50–65 for a big rock rhythm.
Sol 100 LD is the same amp's lead channel.

312.about: German precision: a dense, focused high gain with a tight low end and a lot of clarity on chords.
tips: Gain 55–70; Middle around 50 keeps chords defined.
Dizzy VH+ (Smart Box) is channel 4, more gain.

313.about: A loud, aggressive German high-gain head with a strong upper mid and a percussive low end.
tips: Put the Scream drive in front, Gain 0, Volume up.

314.about: The lead channel of a 90s metal icon: saturated, fat and aggressive, with a lot of gain on tap.
tips: Gain 45–60 is plenty; above it gets fizzy.

315.about: The famous lead channel: smooth, singing sustain with a thick midrange.
tips: Sol 100 OD for the crunch channel.

316.about: The Rectifier's vintage mode: more midrange and a looser, warmer feel than the modern mode.
tips: Calif DualM is the same amp, tighter and scooped.

317.about: Thick, saturated and aggressive, with a huge low end: the classic 90s and 2000s metal rhythm sound.
tips: Gain 60–70; more gain gets fizzy, not heavier.
Put the Scream drive in front with Gain 0 and Volume up.

318.about: A modern German metal head: very high gain, very tight, with a bright, cutting edge.

319.about: A modern take on the hot-rodded British sound: big, saturated and articulate.
tips: Flyman B1 (Smart Box) is the BE channel.

320.about: The Ecstasy's high-gain channel: smooth, rich and singing, with a refined top end.
320.heardOn: Rock and fusion leads, modern rock rhythm.

321.about: The rock bass head: deep, round lows and a gritty growl when pushed. Mid Freq picks where the Middle knob works.
tips: Low for warmth, high for definition in a dense mix.

322.about: A vintage British bass amp: warm, simple and woody, with a gentle drive when pushed.
tips: Up a little to keep the notes clear.

323.about: A boutique clean: full, sweet and dynamic, it reacts to every change in pick attack.
tips: Doctor OD is the same amp, driven.

324.about: The BE channel: a hot-rodded British crunch, tight and punchy, with less gain than the HBE.
324.heardOn: Hard rock, classic rock with more gain.
tips: Flyman B1+ is the HBE channel.

325.about: A legendary lead amp: tight, focused and singing, with a pronounced midrange.
tips: Gain 55–70; Bass under 45 keeps it tight.
The original's V-shaped graphic EQ: try Middle 35.

326.about: Two cascaded gain stages, each with its own tone control.
tips: Gain1 / Tone1 set the first stage, Gain2 / Tone2 the second.

327.about: A rich, warm clean with a lot of body; it starts to break up nicely when pushed.

328.about: The Ecstasy's mid-gain channel: a rich crunch with a strong, warm midrange.
tips: Bog XT V for the high-gain channel.

329.about: A raw, vintage clean with a lot of character; it starts to break up early.
tips: Superb OD is the same amp, driven.

330.about: The 90s Marshall: more gain and a looser low end than the JCM800, built for heavier rock.

331.about: A warm, refined American clean with a lot of headroom and a smooth top end.

332.about: The VH4's lead channel: very high gain, thick and singing, still with a tight low end.

333.about: A big all-tube bass amp: punchy, warm and very full, with a lot of headroom.
tips: Up for a bass that cuts through guitars.

334.about: The Mark IV's lead channel: saturated and focused, a very tight low end and a vocal midrange.
tips: Try Middle 35 for the classic V-curve.

335.about: A thick, warm British drive with a lot of low mids; heavy but never harsh.
tips: Keep it up: the thickness is the point.

336.about: The single-channel version of the classic late-60s head: punchy, open and crunchy.
tips: Brit 50JP is the same amp with the channels linked.

337.about: A raw, vintage overdrive: compressed, hairy and full of character.
tips: Superb CL is the clean side.

338.about: A boutique overdrive: open, dynamic and harmonically rich.
tips: Doctor CL is the clean side.

401.about: A tiny practice-amp speaker: mid-heavy, boxy and lo-fi, great for recording-style tones.

402.about: Sweet and focused, a little bigger than the 1x8; a classic studio clean cab.

403.about: Open, balanced and airy: a versatile 1x12 for cleans and light crunch.

404.about: Bright, sweet and very open: the classic chime cab.

405.about: Warm and full with a soft top end; the natural cab for the tweed amps.

406.about: Open and airy, wide spread, firm but not boomy lows.

407.about: Smooth and full, with a polished American top end.

408.about: Clean, crisp and flat: built for the solid-state Jazz Chorus sound.

409.about: The British Greenback voice in a smaller box: warm mids, less low end than the 4x12.

410.about: Warm, woody and a little compressed, with a strong low-mid thump. The Greenbacks soften the highs, so high-gain amps sound smooth instead of fizzy.

411.about: Tight and modern with a strong upper mid; made for high gain.

412.about: Deep and very tight, with an aggressive, defined top: the German high-gain cab.

413.about: Punchy and scooped, with a big low end; the classic metal cab.

414.about: Balanced and punchy, with a smooth top end for leads.

415.about: Deep, punchy lows and an aggressive upper mid. Built for high gain.

421.about: Punchy and focused, a tight bass cab with a clear attack.

427.basedOn: the Amphonix 2 factory bass cab Mark210 (a 2x10 bass cabinet)
427.about: The Amphonix 2's own compact 2x10 bass cab (stock on the Amphonix 2 only).

428.basedOn: the Amphonix 2 factory bass cab Ampg410 (a 4x10 bass cabinet)
428.about: The Amphonix 2's own 4x10 bass cab (stock on the Amphonix 2 only).
